title: Output accuracy under device mismatch (Monte Carlo, sky130A tt_mm)
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Output" row (1.8V +-2%, i.e. 1.764V-1.836V) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 and revised by #22 (current limit / soft start) and #25/#36 (current-mirror-OTA rail-to-rail output stage plus sized Miller compensation) (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch) under per-instance device mismatch, at a single representative operating point (nominal VIN=3.3V/27C/tt process corner, I_LOAD=1mA light load -- the same light-load convention sim/psrr-dc/ already uses). That row is ratified by issue #1 / DR-006, and the bound cited below is the ratified row's own window, not an invented final limit. This is a mismatch-only statistical check (klt sim's monte_carlo.vary="mismatch"): it re-runs this one PVT point N times with a fresh per-instance AGAUSS mismatch draw each time (sky130A's tt_mm .lib section -- see sim/README.md and docs/cli/sim.md in 2AMLogic/klayout-tools), NOT a re-run across the full PVT corner matrix (that is corner-run.py's separate job, e.g. sim/dropout-vs-load). Initial-condition contract (#164): the transient starts from the block's disabled state (all nodes 0, EN low) and powers up through its own soft-start ramp, the same enable-edge convention sim/startup uses -- it does NOT start from an unconstrained ngspice `.op`. That `.op` is not a physically realizable state of this block: on this very sample sequence it warned on 43/200 draws and on 12 of them handed the transient a start state with FB at 668-1984 V (up to 1.3e15 V) while VOUT sat at VIN -- FB above the only node feeding it through a passive resistor string, which the sky130 poly-resistor model's non-monotone voltage-coefficient term admits as a numerical solution and a transient then holds flat. See design/README.md "#164" for the measurement and the four-variant screen. Known-remaining-gaps caveat (design/README.md "Known gaps / follow-on scope"): the #25/#36 revision closed the unsized-compensation and error-amplifier output-swing-ceiling gaps that dominated the #18-era records, but the pass device's own light-load pole and the absent Iq budget remain open, so a FAIL here is an honest finding about the current design state, not a harness defect.

mc_corner.note: tt_mm is sky130A's mismatch-enabled 'typical' .lib section (MC_MM_SWITCH=1, MC_PR_SWITCH=0 -- per-instance AGAUSS draws on vth0/tox terms, gated by mismatch_factor and scaled 1/sqrt(L*W*mult), confirmed present for both sky130_fd_pr__nfet_g5v0d10v5 and sky130_fd_pr__pfet_g5v0d10v5 -- the two device families this schematic actually instantiates -- by grepping libs.tech/combined/continuous/models_fet.spice at the pinned PDK commit). Single process/temp/supply point: this experiment samples mismatch, not global process/PVT spread (MC_PR_SWITCH=0 in _mm sections).

mc_analysis.note: `uic` (added by #164) makes the transient start from a physically realizable initial condition -- every node at 0, EN low, the block disabled -- and power up through its own soft-start ramp when this testbench's EN edge arrives at 100us, rather than from an unconstrained ngspice operating-point solve. Without it (and with the pre-#164 DC-high EN), the `.op` that seeds the transient has no initial condition at all: on this same 200-draw sequence it emitted 61 solver warnings across 43 samples (`singular matrix` at xldo.fb / xldo.xr_fb_b.t2 / xldo.xr_cz.t1, `dynamic gmin stepping failed`), 3 samples produced no measurement, and 12 settled with VOUT pinned at VIN and FB at 668-1984 V (one at 1.3e15 V) -- FB ABOVE the VOUT node that is the only thing feeding it through a passive resistor string, so not a circuit state. `sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po`'s voltco term (bp2=-0.1228, bq2=1.304) admits it: measured, one W=0.42/L=180um leg's modelled resistance falls 1.04Mohm -> 800ohm between 1V and 1800V and its fitted rbody multiplier crosses zero near 1.32kV (L=52um, R_CZ: ~440V). The state is reproducible with NOMINAL devices from a hostile `.nodeset`, so mismatch is not its trigger -- it only perturbs which branch Newton finds. With any physically realizable start (this `uic` bench; `uic` with EN DC-high; or an `.ic`-at-1.8V-seeded `.op`) all 200 draws regulate to within ~1uV of each other and no sample reports any solver diagnostic. See design/README.md "#164" for the four-variant screen; the 185 samples that already regulated move by at most 17uV (<10ppm).

mc_measurements.name: vout_ss
mc_measurements.spice: .meas tran vout_ss avg v(vout) from=2.5m to=3m
mc_measurements.note: Steady-state VOUT, averaged over the settled tail (2.5ms-3ms of a 3ms transient) of a fixed-1mA-load, VIN=3.3V/27C/tt_mm operating point, reached by powering the block up from its disabled state (EN edge at 100us, `uic`; see mc_analysis.note and #164) rather than from an unconstrained operating-point solve, which on 12 of these 200 draws was not a circuit state at all. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Output" row, 1.8V +-2% (ratified by issue #1 / DR-006).
